text.title: Growth Loops Procedure
text.summary: Eight steps from the event table to the loop spec: name the four stages and the fuel-back event, declare one loop type, measure each stage transition or flag it, compute k and cycle time, project cohorts with decay over at least 90 days and three cycles, map the bottleneck and rank experiments on it, compute CAC payback with and without loop-sourced users, set the quality guardrail and validate.

step.name: name-the-stages-and-the-fuel-back-event
step.input: The event table; the team's loop diagram; `templates/growth-loop-design.md.j2` as the working canvas.
step.action: Fill `stages.input`, `action`, `output`, `fuel_back` in `templates/growth-loops.spec.md.j2`, each with a tracked `event` and a `unit`. The fuel-back event is where one cycle's output becomes the next cycle's input; its unit must be the input unit.
step.decision-gate: No event exists where an output becomes an input, or the units differ: the design is a funnel; label it so and stop, no projection is written (r-loop-closes-output-into-input).

step.name: declare-one-primary-loop-type
step.input: What the loop consumes: user actions, content, capital or supply.
step.action: Set `loop_type` to exactly one of viral, ugc_search, paid, network_effect, supply_side and `input_source` accordingly. List other loops in `secondary_loops[]` with a note that they are tracked separately.
step.decision-gate: Two types are needed to describe the mechanism: split into two specs; nothing from a secondary loop enters this projection (r-one-primary-loop-type).

step.name: measure-each-stage-transition
step.input: Warehouse queries for the three transitions (input-action, action-output, output-fuel_back).
step.action: For each transition record `event`, `numerator`, `denominator`, `value`, `basis` measured with `measured_on` and `sample_size`. A transition with no event or no data is `basis: assumption` with `measured_on` and `sample_size` null.
step.decision-gate: A benchmark or "typical" rate written as measured: reclassify it as an assumption; the projection headline will have to say so (r-stage-conversion-measured-not-estimated).

step.name: compute-k-and-cycle-time
step.input: `stage_metrics[]`; the median days from input event to fuel-back event.
step.action: Set `efficiency.k` to the product of the three values (two decimals) and `cycle_time_days` to the median. If k is below 1, `reading` is amplifier and `multiplier` = 1 / (1 - k); if k is 1 or more, `reading` is self_sustaining and `growth_rate_per_cycle` = k - 1.
step.decision-gate: Any text in the spec calling a k-below-1 loop self-sustaining or viral: rewrite it as an amplifier of external inputs (r-loop-efficiency-and-cycle-time).

step.name: project-cohorts-with-decay
step.input: `efficiency`, the expected external inputs per cycle, and the decay mechanism for the loop type (contributor churn, content decay, audience saturation, rising CPMs).
step.action: Set `projection.horizon_days` (at least 90 and at least three cycle times), `cycles`, `decay.kind` and `rate_per_cycle`. Build `cohorts[]` cycle by cycle: `loop_inputs` = previous total x k x (1 - decay)^(cycle - 1), `total_inputs` = external + loop. Set `rests_on_assumption` when any stage is an assumption and say so in `headline`.
step.decision-gate: The first cycle extrapolated linearly, no decay term, or fewer than three cycles: rebuild; the projection is invalid as written (r-steady-state-projection-90-days).

step.name: map-the-bottleneck-and-rank-experiments
step.action: Set `friction_map.bottleneck_stage` to the transition with the lowest value, `bottleneck_value`, and `k_if_doubled` = 2 x k. Rank `experiments[]` with the bottleneck experiment at rank 1; any experiment on another stage carries a `justification` for preceding a bottleneck experiment.
step.decision-gate: The rank-1 experiment targets the stage the team owns rather than the bottleneck: re-rank or justify in writing (r-friction-map-names-the-bottleneck).

step.name: compute-cac-payback-with-and-without-loop
step.input: Spend and new-user counts for `period_days`; users carrying the fuel-back event.
step.action: Set `cac_payback.attributed_by` to `stages.fuel_back.event`. Compute `without_loop` (blended CAC and payback excluding loop-attributed users) and `with_loop` (including them). Organic and direct traffic stay external inputs.
step.decision-gate: Loop-sourced users counted by channel label instead of the event: recompute; the payback claim is not evidenced (r-cac-payback-with-and-without-loop).

step.name: set-the-quality-guardrail-and-validate
step.input: Activation and D30 retention of the loop-sourced cohort and the baseline cohort (or index and traffic share for content loops).
step.action: Set `quality_guardrail.metric`, a numeric `threshold` (baseline minus the agreed margin), `loop_cohort_value`, `baseline_value` and `status`. Run `scripts/validate-growth-loops.py --file` on the spec.
step.decision-gate: `status` breached: the loop optimisation that caused it is reverted even if k improved; the validator's k, bottleneck or cohort findings are fixed in the spec, not argued (r-loop-quality-guardrail).

list.item: Spec validates via `scripts/validate-growth-loops.py` with no violation.
The fuel-back event is tracked and in the input unit; every stage rate is measured with a date and sample, or flagged and surfaced in the headline.
k, cycle time, the 90-day three-cycle projection with decay, the bottleneck-first experiment ranking, payback with and without loop, and the numeric guardrail are all present and mutually consistent.
